Vendor Portal

Complete guide to the FindMyFlowers Business web portal at vendors.findmyflowers.pl for flower shop owners and freelance florists: sign-up, dashboard, bouquets, smart vases and live connection status, orders, stock, payments, analytics, billing and settings.

FindMyFlowers Business · Web

Authentication

Sign In

Go to vendors.findmyflowers.pl, enter your vendor username and password and click Sign In. Use Forgot password? to reset your password or Create a vendor account to register. The same account works in the FindMyFlowers Business mobile app.

Reset Password

Enter the email address on your account and click Send reset link. A password-reset link is emailed to you. Back to sign in returns to the login page.

Account Registration (Self Sign-Up)

Create Your Vendor Account

The four-step wizard starts a 14-day free trial with no charge until the trial ends.

1. Business: vendor type (Traditional flower shop or Freelance florist), business name, description, contact email and phone, and the shop address with map coordinates. 2. Billing: the billing address used for invoices. 3. Payment: an optional card captured securely by Stripe (it can be skipped and added later from Billing). 4. Confirm: choose a username and password, accept the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy, and click Create account & start trial.

You are signed in straight away. Self-registered vendors may stay pending approval until a platform administrator approves the account; you can set up your shop meanwhile.

Dashboard

Dashboard Overview

After signing in you see Welcome back, {your business} with three tiles: Online vases (vases that sent a heartbeat in the last five minutes, out of all registered), Available bouquets and Pending orders.

Needs your attention collects what to act on: Offline devices (Check devices), stock items that are low or empty (Check stock) and freshness price suggestions (Review prices). Below are Recent bouquet activity and My vases with each vase's live connection badge.

The left sidebar opens every section: Dashboard, My Bouquets, My Vases, Orders, Stock, Payments, Billing, Feedback, Analytics and Settings, plus Contact us and Logout at the bottom. On a phone-sized screen the sidebar becomes a bottom bar with a More page.

Bouquet Management

My Bouquets

Lists all bouquets as cards with photo, name, price, availability, freshness rating and date. Search by name, filter with All / Available, and see totals (Total, Available, Draft) at the bottom.

When a bouquet has been on display for a while, an amber Freshness suggestion proposes a lower price (for example Reduce to PLN 9.30, −70% after 72h). Click Accept to apply it in one step, or ignore it.

Create a New Bouquet

Click Create New Bouquet and pick the vase the bouquet is in (Create Here). The vase page opens in upload mode: upload a photo, then set the price to make the bouquet available to customers.

Set / Change Price & Freshness Rating

Change Price opens the price dialog. Enter the price in PLN and choose a Freshness rating: Not shown, or 1–3 flowers for the number of days the bouquet is guaranteed fresh. Customers see it as flower pictograms on the map; it drops by one flower a day and never changes the price.

Click Set Price to save. A bouquet without a price becomes available for purchase once priced.

Customer Preview

Customer preview shows the bouquet as customers see it: photo, name, price, availability and freshness.

Delete a Bouquet

The red bin button asks for confirmation before deleting a bouquet. Deleting cannot be undone.

Smart Vase Management

My Smart Vases

Tiles count Online, Offline and Total registered vases. The table lists each device with its location, installation status, Connection badge, current bouquet, last heartbeat (UTC) and actions: View details and + (create a bouquet on that vase).

Connection status updates live while the page is open: a vase is Online when it sent a heartbeat within the last five minutes, otherwise Offline, and a notification pops up when a vase goes offline or comes back. Use Order new vases and My vase orders for hardware orders.

Vase Details — Online Vase

Device Information shows the device ID, installation status, health, connection and last heartbeat. Sensor Data shows temperature, humidity, the bouquet's state and price, how long it has been available and the last update. Vase Location shows the address and coordinates. On the right, Current Bouquet shows the photo customers see and lets you upload a new one (JPG, PNG or GIF, max 5 MB).

Vase Details — Offline Vase

An offline vase shows Health: Critical, Connection: Offline and how long ago its last heartbeat arrived. A warning says the last readings may be stale. Check the device's power and Wi-Fi connection before acting on them.

Upload a New Bouquet Photo

Opened from Create New Bouquet or the + button. Choose the bouquet photo and click Upload Bouquet Photo; then set the price on My Bouquets to make it available to customers.

Vase Ordering

Order Smart Vases

From My Vases → Order new vases, choose a quantity (1–10 per order), enter the shipping address and optional notes, and click Place Order. The platform team reviews the order and ships the hardware. No payment is taken here.

My Vase Orders

Tracks every vase order with its date, quantity, status (Requested → Confirmed → Shipped → Delivered) and the courier tracking number once shipped.

Order Management

My Orders

Customer orders with their status, payment state, number of items, total and date. Search the loaded orders or filter by status: All, Paid, Preparing, Ready, In Delivery, Completed, Cancelled. Click View for details.

Order Details

Shows the order status, customer, creation date, total and payment state, and each item with its unit price and the customer's review. For active orders the Actions panel moves the order forward: Accept & Prepare → Ready for Pickup or Start Delivery → Mark Delivered, or Cancel Order.

Stock NEW

Stock Overview

Flowers, greenery and materials on hand. Tiles count all items, low-stock and out-of-stock items, and the total stock value at the latest unit costs. Search and filter by kind (Flower, Greenery, Material) and status, optionally including archived items. The table shows quantity, alert level, status, unit cost, value, supplier and last delivery; click Manage on a row to open that item. Use Add item and Activity at the top.

Add Stock Item

Choose the kind, enter the name, optional colour, the unit it is counted in (flowers and greenery are always counted in stems), optional unit cost, low-stock alert level, supplier and notes, plus the quantity on hand now (recorded as opening stock). Click Add to stock.

Stock Item Details

Shows quantity, status, unit cost, value, alert level and last delivery. Update stock records what happened: Received (a delivery, and its unit cost becomes the current cost), Used, Wasted or Count (a stock-take that sets the exact quantity), with an optional note. Edit changes the item's details and Archive item hides it. History lists every change with the quantity after it.

Stock Activity

All stock changes across every item, newest first: when, which item, what happened, the change and the quantity after it, with notes.

Count Stock from Photos

On Stock, click Count stock from photos and add 1–5 photos of your bench or cold room. The AI estimates how many of each item you have and links what it recognises to your stock items. Review the list: each line shows the photo or kind icon, colour swatches, the quantity on record (Now) and the counted quantity with the change. Lines marked Please check are the ones the AI was least sure of. Link unrecognised lines to an item (or use Create item), adjust the counts, untick anything you don't want to change and press Apply counts. Nothing changes your stock before that; the ticked lines are written as stock counts in Stock Activity in one go. Uses one of your monthly stock photo recognitions.

AI Florist: Start from My Stock

In the AI Florist wizard, click Start from my stock. On the left are your stock items as cards with photo, kind icon (flower, leaf or ribbon), colour swatches, quantity and cost; filter them by kind, colour or text. Drag a card into Starting set on the right — or use its Add button, press Enter on a focused card, or tick several cards and click Add selected. Each card adds up to 5 stems (1 for materials); adding it again adds more, and you can change quantities in the set. A quantity above what's in stock shows a warning but is allowed. The set is saved as you go, so you can leave and come back. Click Use as my stock to check the lines in the table (photos, kind icons and colour swatches; empty prices show the stock cost or remembered price that will be used), then confirm and choose your design. Counting stock from photos now lives on the Stock page.

AI Florist: Reconstruct a Bouquet

In the AI Florist wizard, click Reconstruct a bouquet from photos — for example when a customer sends a picture of a bouquet they like. Add 1–5 photos of that one bouquet and click Analyse bouquet (uses one of your monthly photo recognitions). The wizard lists what the bouquet seems to be made of and matches each item to your stock with a match score: In your stock, Not enough in stock and Missing. Stem counts are estimates. Use Change on a line to pick another of your stock items, mark it Not in my stock, or change the number needed. Under To buy for this bouquet, Copy list or Download CSV gives you the missing items (ordering from suppliers is coming later). Click Use matched items to design recipes from what you have — one recipe stays close to the photo and one suggests the best substitutes. Nothing here changes your stock levels.

AI Florist: Cost Assessor

In the AI Florist wizard, click What does this bouquet cost me?. Add 1–5 photos of one finished bouquet and an optional note (for example "hidden: 3 eucalyptus inside"), then click Analyse and price (uses one of your monthly cost assessments). Each line shows the item, your matching stock item, the likely quantity with a min/max for hidden stems, and the price used: stock cost, remembered price, your price or price missing. Change the stock item, quantities or price, add a missed item in the last row or tick Remove, then click Save and recalculate; tick Remember to keep a price for next time. The cost shows flowers, materials, labour and overhead from your Cost settings, the total with a range, and a suggested price at your target margin (set it in Cost settings, default 60 %). Enter a selling price to see your margin. Under What next? you can Deduct from stock for a bouquet you have already made, Open in AI Florist to design similar recipes, set the price on one of your bouquets, or Print the summary. Nothing happens to your stock unless you click Deduct.

Payments

Payments

Payment activity over the last 30 days: paid orders, failed payments, refunds, disputes, refund rate and payment method mix. The table lists orders that need money-related attention, filterable by Needs refund retry, Disputed, Refund failed and Reconciliation drift.

Feedback

Customer Feedback

Reviews customers left on their orders. Choose a Min rating and click Filter; Reset clears it.

Analytics

Analytics Dashboard

Business performance: total revenue, total orders, bouquets sold, average order value, online vases out of all registered, and available bouquets.

Settings

Profile Settings

Sign-in Account shows the email you sign in with and whether it is verified. It is used for sign-in, verification and password resets and is separate from the business contact email. Use sign-in email copies it into the contact email field.

Business Information: edit the business name, description, contact email (shown to customers) and contact phone, then click Save Changes. The Business preview shows your edits before saving. Quick links lead to Opening Hours and back to the dashboard.

Opening Hours

Set the weekly schedule: tick the days you are open and choose opening and closing times. Copy Monday to weekdays fills Tuesday–Friday in one click. Click Save Schedule.

Profile & Settings Hub

The More page (used mostly on small screens) links to Profile Settings, Opening Hours, Stock, My Vases, Order Smart Vases, Vase Orders, Analytics, Payments, Billing & Subscription, Feedback, Contact us and Logout.

Billing & Subscription

Subscription Overview

Shows your platform plan, status, trial countdown, next billing date and the saved payment method, with options to update the payment method or cancel (access continues to the end of the paid period). If no subscription is found, as for this demo vendor, the page says so and offers Contact support and View bouquet payments.

Payment Method & Billing Address

Add or replace the card used for your subscription. Card details go straight into Stripe's secure form and never touch FindMyFlowers servers, and the card is not charged during a free trial. Click Save card. A card already on file is shown at the top, with a Replace card button. The Billing address form is saved separately with Save billing address.

Support

Contact Us

Contact us (sidebar or page footer) opens a form: your reply-to email, a subject and your message. Complete the Verify you are human check and click Send, or use or use your own email app to write from your mail program.

Help NEW

Click Help in the sidebar (or in More on a phone) to open this manual in a new tab, or the ? in the top bar to open it at the section for the page you are on. You are signed in to the documentation with your portal session, so there is no second login; if your session has expired the documentation asks you to sign in and then continues to the same section. The documentation shows vendors only the vendor manuals.

Bouquet Requests

Bouquet Requests

Click Bouquet requests in the sidebar to see what customers near you want: their reference images, note, budget, occasion, wanted time and delivery or pickup. Requests appear when they are inside your service radius around your shop (set it in Request settings) and your platform subscription is active. The location is shown only as a district and an approximate distance — the address, exact pin and the customer's name stay hidden until the customer has paid. Each card shows how many offers have already been sent and when offers close.

Send an Offer

Open a request and fill in Make an offer: your price (PLN, incl. VAT), a delivery fee (leave empty if included), when it will be ready and, for delivery, by when it will arrive, plus notes for the customer (for example substitutions). Click Send offer. You can update the offer (each change is a new version the customer sees), add up to 5 images or Withdraw it. Times up to 2 hours later than requested are allowed and marked later than requested. Click Reconstruct with AI Florist to open the request's images in the AI Florist reconstruction (what's in stock, what's missing, an estimated cost and a draft offer note to copy). If the customer edits the request, your offer is marked the customer changed the request.

Custom Orders

When the customer accepts your offer, they have 30 minutes to pay. After payment the request shows Your custom order with the address, recipient, a map link and the due time. Move it along with the phase buttons (In progress, Ready, Out for delivery, Delivered or Picked up). If you need more time, use Need more time? to propose a new time with a reason; the customer can accept, or cancel with a full refund when it is more than an hour later; an unanswered proposal is accepted after 30 minutes. The order also appears under Orders marked Custom; its status is changed only on the request page. You get alerts before the start time, when it isn't ready and when it is late.

Request Settings and Inbox

Request settings sets your service radius (1–50 km), preparation lead time, new-request alerts, quiet hours and a minimum budget. The Inbox lists all request alerts — new requests, accepted and rejected offers, payments, time changes and late orders — with Mark all read.

Selling Online Only

Selling Online Only

Choose Online only, delivery to customers when you have no shop counter and no collections: in the sign-up step How do you sell?, or later in Settings under How do you sell?. Online-only vendors don't use smart vases, so the My Vases menu, the vase tiles on the dashboard and the vase-ordering prompts are hidden. You can switch to online only once you have no smart vases (return them first); switching back to in-store with smart vases is always possible.

Add an Online Bouquet

Click + in the top bar or Add online bouquet on My Bouquets. Add a clear photo of the finished bouquet (customers can't see it in person), a name, the price in PLN, how many days it stays fresh (1–3) and the flowers in it, then click List for delivery. The bouquet appears on the customer map at once as Delivery only, with your location shown only approximately. It is one physical bouquet: it sells once. From an AI Florist recipe, List online fills the form in for you.

Online Listings and Orders

My Bouquets marks online listings with an Online · delivery only badge and a countdown. A listing comes off the map when its freshness runs out (or after 3 days at most) unless it sells first. Use Change Price to re-price it and Remove listing to take it off the map (not possible while a customer is paying for it). Orders for online listings are always delivered: move them through Preparing, In delivery and Delivered in Orders; there is no Ready for pickup step and no vase to reset.

How Sure Is the AI?

What the Label Means

Wherever the AI recognises flowers from your photos (AI Florist → Reconstruct a bouquet, the photo stock check and Stock → Count stock from photos) each line shows how often answers like it turned out to be right when florists checked them. The AI's own "90 % sure" is no longer shown: it said that about almost everything. The label has four states: Usually right · 41 checks, Check this · right 7 of 10 times, Often wrong · check it and New: not enough checks yet. Hover over it to see whether it comes from your own checks or from florists across the platform. Lines that are often wrong are listed first, are never linked to your stock automatically, and a count that is often wrong makes the Cost Assessor show a wider cost range. It is a track record, not a guarantee.

Right, Wrong or Not Sure

Under each recognised line, press ✓ Right when the AI named the flower correctly, ✗ Wrong to say what it really is (pick from your stock names or the list, e.g. Scabiosa instead of Astrantia) or Not in the bouquet when it isn't there at all, and ? when you're not sure. This is about what the flower is, not whether you have it: Not in my stock under Change stays separate. A different colour or variety still counts as right for the flower; just correct it in the line. Confirming the list (Use matched items, Confirm stock, Apply counts, saving a cost assessment) also counts as a light check of the lines you kept. Your answers are remembered: a correction you give twice becomes a hint for your next photos. Each verdict reloads the list, so give your verdicts before you edit quantities.

What Is Shared

By default your checks also help other shops: only anonymous counts per flower type are shared (for example "carnations: checked 12 times, right 9"), never your shop's name, photos, notes, prices or stock, and a count is only used once at least three shops contributed. Your own corrections and hints stay in your shop. To stop sharing, open AI Florist → House style and switch off Help improve recognition for everyone; your checks then only tune the labels for your shop, and you still see the platform's numbers.

What the Pictures Mean

Three Pictures per Line

In AI Florist → Reconstruct a bouquet and in the Cost Assessor each line can show up to three small pictures. In your photo is the part of your photo the AI means — click it to see the whole photo with that flower marked. Looks like is a reference photo of the flower the AI named (or of its variety, e.g. seeded eucalyptus), so you can compare at a glance. Your stock is the photo of the stock item it was matched to. A line without a picture of your photo shows the flower/greenery/material pictogram instead: the AI couldn't point at it (hidden fillers, for example). The pictures of your photos are private to your shop and are deleted with the design, like the photos themselves.

Could Be, Look-alikes and Your Stock

Could be: Eucalyptus 'Seeded' appears when the AI named only the flower and that flower has a very common variety. Press Use it to rename the line; it is matched to your stock again and counts as "the AI was right". Where image matching is switched on you may also see AI says Astilbe, the photo looks like Amaranthus: the picture resembles another flower more than the one the AI named. Press It's Amaranthus to rename it (this tells us the AI was wrong) or It's Astilbe to confirm the AI. Your stock may have this: Rose 'Freedom' means your own stock photo looks like this line although the name didn't match — press Use it to link it. Nothing is ever changed without your tap, and Undo under a renamed line goes back to the AI's name. In What is it? the suggestions now list the atlas names in English and Polish first, then your stock names.

Where the Reference Photos Come From

The "Looks like" photos come from our flower atlas of about 150 cut flowers and greenery. They are taken only from Wikimedia Commons and iNaturalist under licences that allow commercial use (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA), or are our own photos, and each one is checked by our team first. Hover over a reference photo to see its author and licence, and click it to open its source. The full list of credits is under Image credits in the page footer.
